subject: Human Evolution
title: The Laetoli Footprints
description: A fast breakdown of The Laetoli Footprints for builders.

hook.text: In 1978, Mary Leakey's team found footprints preserved in volcanic ash in Tanzania—3.6 million years old.

buildup.text: Two or three individuals walked across fresh ash from a nearby eruption. Rain cemented the prints.

discovery.text: The prints show a modern heel-to-toe gait, proving bipedalism existed long before stone tools or big brains.

twist.text: One set of prints appears to pause and turn—a fleeting moment of curiosity frozen for 3.6 million years.

climax.text: No bones, no tools—just footprints that prove upright walking with more certainty than any skeleton.

punchline.text: The best evidence of walking is a walk.

quiz.question: What do the Laetoli footprints prove?
